sources: Cambridge Economic History of Europe vol. II
Wikipedia articles on the individual cities

trade_hubs.name: Bruges
trade_hubs.notes: Hub of the Flemish cloth trade and chief Hanseatic Kontor in the west; Italian galleys call yearly. Declines after the Zwin silts up (late 15th c.).

trade_hubs.name: Lübeck
trade_hubs.notes: Head of the Hanseatic League; salt from Lüneburg westward, Baltic grain, furs and wax eastward.

trade_hubs.name: Venice
trade_hubs.notes: Mistress of the Levant trade: spices, silk and cotton through the state galley convoys (mude).

trade_hubs.name: Genoa
trade_hubs.notes: Rival of Venice; Black Sea colonies (Pera, Caffa), alum of Phocaea, Atlantic galleys to Bruges and England.

trade_hubs.name: Constantinople
trade_hubs.notes: Gate between the Black Sea and the Mediterranean, its trade now largely in Genoese and Venetian hands.

trade_hubs.name: Alexandria
trade_hubs.notes: Main Mediterranean outlet of the Red Sea spice route under the Mamluks; Venetian and Genoese fondaci.

trade_hubs.name: Cairo
trade_hubs.notes: Largest city of the Islamic world; Karimi merchants dominate the Indian Ocean spice trade.

trade_hubs.name: Novgorod
trade_hubs.notes: Hanseatic Peterhof; furs, wax and silver of the Russian north exchanged for Flemish cloth.

trade_hubs.name: Champagne Fairs (Troyes)
trade_hubs.notes: Former clearing house of European trade, in steep decline since c.1300 as the sea route to Bruges takes over.

trade_hubs.name: Cologne
trade_hubs.notes: Largest German city; Rhine wine and metalwork; staple right on all Rhine traffic.

trade_hubs.name: Paris
trade_hubs.notes: Largest city of Latin Europe; luxury crafts and the Seine trade of the Hanse of the water-merchants.

trade_hubs.name: London
trade_hubs.notes: Wool and later cloth exports; Hanseatic Steelyard and Italian merchants.

trade_hubs.name: Barcelona
trade_hubs.notes: Catalan Mediterranean commerce with Sicily, Sardinia, North Africa and the Levant; Consulate of the Sea.

trade_hubs.name: Seville
trade_hubs.notes: Oil, wine and Genoese finance; later the monopoly port for the Indies (1503).

trade_hubs.name: Lisbon
trade_hubs.notes: Atlantic port with a Genoese colony; becomes the hub of the Guinea and India trade after 1450–1500.

trade_hubs.name: Antwerp
trade_hubs.notes: Brabant fairs town; becomes the leading market of northern Europe c.1450–1560.

trade_hubs.name: Amsterdam
trade_hubs.notes: Small Holland port in 1356; dominant entrepôt of Europe from c.1580.

trade_hubs.name: Nuremberg
trade_hubs.notes: Imperial city of metalworkers and long-distance merchants linking Venice and the north.

trade_hubs.name: Frankfurt am Main
trade_hubs.notes: Imperial fairs in spring and autumn; book fair later.

trade_hubs.name: Vienna
trade_hubs.notes: Staple right on the Danube route to Hungary.

trade_hubs.name: Prague
trade_hubs.notes: Imperial residence under Charles IV; silver of Kutná Hora.

trade_hubs.name: Kraków
trade_hubs.notes: Royal Polish capital; copper of Hungary, salt of Wieliczka, route to Lemberg and the Black Sea.

trade_hubs.name: Buda
trade_hubs.notes: Royal seat of Hungary; gold florins from Kremnitz, cattle and wine.

trade_hubs.name: Ragusa
trade_hubs.notes: Dalmatian republic trading Balkan silver and lead to Italy.

trade_hubs.name: Tana
trade_hubs.notes: Venetian–Genoese post at the mouth of the Don, terminus of the overland silk road via Sarai.

trade_hubs.name: Caffa
trade_hubs.notes: Genoese capital of the Black Sea trade: slaves, grain, furs and silk.

trade_hubs.name: Trebizond
trade_hubs.notes: Black Sea outlet of the Tabriz caravan road.

trade_hubs.name: Tabriz
trade_hubs.notes: Former Ilkhanid capital, great silk and caravan market between Persia, Anatolia and the Black Sea.

trade_hubs.name: Aleppo
trade_hubs.notes: Caravan city between Iraq, Anatolia and the Syrian coast.

trade_hubs.name: Damascus
trade_hubs.notes: Mamluk Syria's metropolis; spices via Beirut, Hajj caravans, steel and textiles.

trade_hubs.name: Beirut
trade_hubs.notes: Port of Damascus where Venetian galleys load spices.

trade_hubs.name: Tunis
trade_hubs.notes: Hafsid capital; Italian and Catalan fondouks; Saharan gold and wool.

trade_hubs.name: Fez
trade_hubs.notes: Marinid capital; leather, textiles and the northern end of the trans-Saharan gold road.

trade_hubs.name: Sijilmasa
trade_hubs.notes: Old Saharan gateway oasis, past its peak.

trade_hubs.name: Timbuktu
trade_hubs.notes: Mali's Niger-bend market for gold, salt and books.

trade_hubs.name: Gao
trade_hubs.notes: Songhai trading city on the Niger.

trade_hubs.name: Kilwa
trade_hubs.notes: Swahili sultanate controlling the gold of Sofala.

trade_hubs.name: Mogadishu
trade_hubs.notes: Swahili–Somali textile and ivory port described by Ibn Battuta.

trade_hubs.name: Aden
trade_hubs.notes: Rasulid entrepôt between India and the Red Sea.

trade_hubs.name: Hormuz
trade_hubs.notes: Island kingdom controlling the Gulf trade with India.

trade_hubs.name: Basra
trade_hubs.notes: Old Gulf port of Iraq, much reduced since the Mongol conquest.

trade_hubs.name: Baghdad
trade_hubs.notes: Jalayirid capital, recovering slowly since 1258.

trade_hubs.name: Bergen
trade_hubs.notes: Hanseatic Bryggen; Norwegian stockfish for grain.

trade_hubs.name: Visby
trade_hubs.notes: Gotland's walled trading town, early centre of Baltic commerce.

trade_hubs.name: Stockholm
trade_hubs.notes: Swedish iron and copper exports, run largely by German burghers.

trade_hubs.name: Danzig
trade_hubs.notes: Teutonic Order's port for Prussian and Polish grain and timber.

trade_hubs.name: Riga
trade_hubs.notes: Hanseatic gateway up the Daugava to Polotsk and Smolensk.

trade_hubs.name: Reval
trade_hubs.notes: Hanseatic port for the Novgorod trade.

trade_hubs.name: Lemberg
trade_hubs.notes: Polish since 1349; Armenian and Italian merchants on the road to Caffa.

trade_hubs.name: Kiev
trade_hubs.notes: Former Rus metropolis, reduced under Mongol overlordship.

trade_hubs.name: Sarai
trade_hubs.notes: Golden Horde capital on the Volga, hub of the silk road and fur trade.

trade_hubs.name: Hajji Tarkhan (Astrakhan)
trade_hubs.notes: Volga delta market linking the Caspian and the Horde.

trade_hubs.name: Bolghar
trade_hubs.notes: Volga fur market of the north.

trade_hubs.name: Urgench
trade_hubs.notes: Khwarazm's caravan city on the road from Sarai to Central Asia.

trade_hubs.name: Samarkand
trade_hubs.notes: Transoxianan silk and paper market.

trade_hubs.name: Bursa
trade_hubs.notes: Ottoman capital and rising silk market.

trade_hubs.name: Famagusta
trade_hubs.notes: Christian clearing port for Levantine goods since the fall of Acre.

trade_hubs.name: Candia
trade_hubs.notes: Capital of Venetian Crete; wine, grain and a galley base.

trade_hubs.name: Naples
trade_hubs.notes: Angevin capital; grain and silk of the south.

trade_hubs.name: Palermo
trade_hubs.notes: Sicilian grain and sugar.

trade_hubs.name: Florence
trade_hubs.notes: Banking and woollen cloth; the gold florin is the standard coin of Europe.

trade_hubs.name: Milan
trade_hubs.notes: Arms, fustian and Lombard banking under the Visconti.

trade_hubs.name: Palma de Mallorca
trade_hubs.notes: Catalan-Majorcan trade and cartography centre.

trade_hubs.name: Granada
trade_hubs.notes: Nasrid silk and the Genoese-run sugar of Málaga.

trade_hubs.name: Havana
trade_hubs.notes: Later Spanish treasure-fleet harbour (from 1519/1561).

trade_hubs.name: Veracruz
trade_hubs.notes: Later Atlantic port of New Spain (from 1519).

trade_hubs.name: Salvador da Bahia
trade_hubs.notes: Later capital of Portuguese Brazil and sugar port (from 1549).

trade_hubs.name: Elmina
trade_hubs.notes: Later Portuguese gold-trading castle São Jorge da Mina (from 1482).

trade_hubs.name: Luanda
trade_hubs.notes: Later Portuguese slave-trading port in Angola (from 1576).

trade_hubs.name: Cape of Good Hope (Table Bay)
trade_hubs.notes: Later Dutch victualling station (from 1652).
